bullets.text: Retired $223M hybrid debt; declared $1/share extraordinary dividend; repurchased 10.7M shares YTD; variable dividend on track for largest payout yet under 1.65 Gainshare factor; total investment return 3.3% in Q3 (6.5% YTD).

Q3 CR 92.9 reflected meaningful reserve development, closely matching prior-year quarterly performance; net income was quite comparable to Q3 2009 after considering a favorable tax-related item in the prior-year period.
Written premiums +5% YOY in Q3, maintaining Q2 pace and reaching +6% YTD; Personal Lines alone grew closer to 6% in Q3, supported by increasing conversion and customer retention.

Direct auto PIF +14% YOY and Agency auto rose 3%; policy life expectancy increased notably in both channels; Commercial Auto PIF -1%, with management believing large-market growth is needed to recover.

Frequency and severity trends remained manageable, though bodily injury severity continued an unexpected decline that does not easily reconcile with general experience, prompting strong reserving and pricing scrutiny.

Pricing trends remained relatively modest overall; results improved across more challenging personal injury protection (PIP) states, shifting management's focus toward restoring business growth in those jurisdictions.

Independent agents ranked Progressive as the top-rated overall carrier in J.D. Power's Insurance Agency Satisfaction Study, scoring clearly superior across multiple specific carrier dimensions evaluated.

Jeff Charney hired as Chief Marketing Officer from Aflac to lead branding and marketing, with a key objective to build organizational talent depth matching Progressive’s other core business functions.

Progressive increased its standing in J.D. Power’s 2010 National Auto Insurance Study for the seventh consecutive year, though absolute and internal scores indicate significant customer satisfaction improvements remain needed.
The third quarter was perhaps more notable for an absence of significant hurricane activity; with plenty of activity at sea, there was little concern for the family auto.
